tagline: Along the Teche, names carry the migrations.
intro: Out of Catahoula, just beyond the western boundary of the Atchafalaya Basin, the drive reaches St. Martinville on Bayou Teche. Swamp and prairie share the ground here. Farther along, Ruth and Gecko also stand by the bayou, while Cecilia carries a succession of names left by different languages.

St. Martinville once went by Petit Paris, for its good hotels and a French theater, the Duchamp Opera House, founded in 1830. The Evangeline Oak of Longfellow's poem is here too. Up the road, Cecilia remains one of the last strongholds of Cajun French in Louisiana.

moments.title: Catahoula
moments.text: The settlement lies just outside the western boundary of the Atchafalaya River Basin.

moments.title: Saint Martin of Tours Church
moments.text: Founded in 1765 with Acadian refugees, the parish built its present church after an 1820 act let the congregation raise the money by lottery.

moments.title: Cecilia
moments.text: Once called La Punta and La Grande Pointe, the community later shed La Place after its mail became confused with another town's.
